recognize_zh: 箭頭處巨大細胞內有約七個彼此分離、大小一致的橢圓形核，胞質豐富呈藍紫色並散布細小紫紅顆粒、邊緣不規則，這是骨髓抽吸中的破骨細胞（osteoclast），與核分葉相連的巨核細胞不同。
features: Very large multinucleated giant cell with about seven discrete, separate nuclei
Nuclei uniform, round to oval, with fine to moderately clumped chromatin and small nucleoli
Abundant blue-lavender cytoplasm with fine scattered azurophilic granules and a frayed irregular border
No nuclear lobes connected to one another (unlike a megakaryocyte)
Background of maturing granulocytes, erythroid precursors, lymphocytes, a plasma cell and red cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (May-Grünwald-Giemsa) shows a large multinucleated giant cell containing approximately seven separate, uniform oval nuclei with small nucleoli, set in abundant blue-lavender cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules and irregular margins. The surrounding marrow cells show normal-appearing granulocytic and erythroid elements. No atypia is present in the giant cell nuclei. Findings are consistent with a normal osteoclast.

ddx.vs: Megakaryocytes have a single multilobated nucleus with interconnected lobes and pink granular cytoplasm with platelet budding, whereas osteoclast nuclei are completely separate and uniform.
Multinucleated plasma cells have few nuclei with clock-face chromatin in deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm with a hof.

ddx.dx: Tumor giant cells (metastatic carcinoma, Reed-Sternberg cells)
ddx.vs: Tumor giant cells show nuclear pleomorphism, variable nuclear size and large prominent nucleoli rather than uniform bland nuclei.
